title: When opening and randomly using SSMS, the keybindings get into an a degraded state

status.label: Clarify the SSMS and extension conditions
status.detail: The original report lists PowerToys 0.80.1 and says swapped Caps Lock/Ctrl behavior becomes corrupted in SSMS; another user reports the same symptom with DBForge SQL Complete and says it stops when the extension is absent.

judgment.rationale: The original report gives a specific Caps Lock/Ctrl swap and says the key state becomes degraded only in SSMS, but the author cannot reliably reproduce it and is unsure PowerToys is involved. A second user reports the symptom with DBForge SQL Complete and says it works without the extension. The original reporter's current PowerToys/SSMS version and extension conditions are unknown.
evidence: The original report lists PowerToys 0.80.1, SSMS 20.1.10.0, and a Caps Lock/Ctrl (Left) swap.
The reporter says the key state degrades in SSMS and can be temporarily mitigated by pressing Esc, Caps Lock, and the Windows key, but cannot reliably reproduce it.
A second user says the same issue occurs with DBForge SQL Complete and works without that extension; this does not establish that the original reporter uses DBForge.
The issue is open and unassigned; no linked fix was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask the original reporter whether the issue persists on a current release and whether SSMS extensions, especially DBForge SQL Complete, are involved; do not assume the two reports share a root cause.

fix_assessment.rationale: If current builds reproduce the behavior, Keyboard Manager or an SSMS extension may leave a remapped key state active. The extension's apparent role in one report and the original reporter's unreliable reproduction make the mechanism uncertain.

proposed_fixes.title: Prevent SSMS use from corrupting a configured key swap
proposed_fixes.root_cause: An interaction between Keyboard Manager's Caps Lock/Ctrl swap and SSMS or an SSMS extension may leave modifier state inconsistent. Current version and extension involvement are unknown.
plan: Confirm the current PowerToys version and whether DBForge SQL Complete or another SSMS extension is installed.
Reproduce with the Caps Lock/Ctrl swap in SSMS with extensions enabled and disabled.
Capture a fresh diagnostic report immediately after the key state degrades if the behavior still occurs.
Correct the identified state handling or extension interaction and add a focused regression test.
verification: Verify Caps Lock and Ctrl remain correctly swapped through SSMS tab changes and ordinary use.
Verify the issue does not occur with the implicated extension enabled or disabled, as applicable.
Verify unrelated key mappings remain unaffected.

confidence.rationale: The report provides a specific mapping and SSMS context, and another user identifies an extension condition, but neither a current reproduction nor a common mechanism is established.

issue_context.summary: The Caps Lock/Ctrl swap reportedly degrades during SSMS use; a second user associates a similar symptom with DBForge SQL Complete.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.80.1, SSMS 20.1.10.0, and swaps Caps Lock with Ctrl (Left).
The original reporter says the failure is intermittent in SSMS and can be temporarily mitigated with Esc, Caps Lock, and the Windows key.
A second user reports the same symptom with DBForge SQL Complete and says it works without that extension.
inferences: An SSMS extension may be involved, but the second user's report does not establish that it affects the original reporter.
issue_context.analysis: The extension and current-version conditions discriminate an app/extension interaction from Keyboard Manager state loss. The reported workaround is not sufficiently explained to serve as a fix.
initial_investigation: Read the original issue and all comments, including the DBForge SQL Complete report.
No linked fix or exact covering issue was found.

information_gaps.information: Whether the issue persists on current PowerToys and SSMS versions, and whether the original reporter uses DBForge SQL Complete or another SSMS extension
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether the failure is current and whether the extension interaction reported by another user is relevant to the original reproduction.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the current PowerToys and SSMS versions, installed SSMS extensions, and whether disabling the extensions changes the behavior.

actions.label: Confirm current SSMS and extension conditions

comment.body: Thanks for the specific Caps Lock/Ctrl swap and SSMS details. Another user reports that a similar symptom occurs with DBForge SQL Complete and stops when that extension is absent, but it is not clear whether it affects your setup. Could you share your current PowerToys and SSMS versions, list any SSMS extensions, and say whether disabling them changes the behavior?
